title: Derivative of a profile pair derivative
statement: Let $U$ be the Gaussian isoperimetric profile and $Q$ the total Gaussian quantile. For $a,t,k\in\mathbb R$ with $a+t,a-t\in(0,1)$, the function $x\mapsto-2U(a+x)Q(a+x)+2kU(a-x)Q(a-x)$ is differentiable at $t$, with derivative $2\bigl(Q(a+t)^2+kQ(a-t)^2-1-k\bigr)$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. If $a,t,k\in\mathbb R$ and $a\pm t\in(0,1)$, then the derivative at $t$ of $x\mapsto-2I(a+x)Q(a+x)+2kI(a-x)Q(a-x)$ is $2(Q(a+t)^2+kQ(a-t)^2-1-k)$.
